items.title: SQL Injection
items.description: User-controlled input is built into a SQL string passed to .execute() (request input -> query string). Bound parameters do not sanitize an interpolated query string.
items.codeSnippet: rows = con.execute(f"SELECT * FROM {table}").fetchall()  # table from whitelist
items.fixSuggestion: Use bound parameters: execute('... WHERE x = %s', (value,)) or the ORM query builder; never f-string/%/.format user input into SQL.

vision.summary: Product-engineering vision signals look strong: observability + analytics + feature flags wired up.

findings.title: No observability stack detected
findings.description: No APM (OpenTelemetry/Datadog/NewRelic/Honeycomb) and no error tracking (Sentry/Rollbar/Bugsnag) dep detected. Without these, you can't correlate user-impacting issues with code changes.
findings.fixSuggestion: Start with Sentry — fastest path to crash/error visibility. Add OpenTelemetry if you need full tracing. Wire up alerts to a notification channel humans actually read.

findings.title: No feature-flag platform
findings.description: Feature flags decouple deploy from release: kill-switch on regressions, staged rollouts to a % of users, A/B test cohorts. Releases without them are all-or-nothing.
findings.fixSuggestion: For early-stage: Posthog (free tier, JS-SDK-only). For larger teams: LaunchDarkly / Statsig. Even a homegrown flags table beats no kill-switch.

findings.title: No product analytics dependency
findings.description: No Posthog / Mixpanel / Amplitude / Segment / Heap / Plausible / Fathom dep detected. Without telemetry on feature adoption + user journeys, you can't close the loop between code shipped and value delivered.
findings.fixSuggestion: PostHog (open source, generous free tier) is the lowest-friction start. Track 3-5 key events: signup, activation, first-value-moment, retention, churn signal.

findings.title: No API versioning convention
findings.description: No `/v1/`, `/v2/` path-prefixed routes detected (as string literals — not comments). Breaking changes will hit every consumer at once.
findings.fixSuggestion: Adopt URL-based versioning (`/v1/users`). Document the deprecation policy in your README.

findings.title: No README found
findings.description: No `README.md` / `README` / `docs/README.md` (case-insensitive) found. Without a top-level README, the project's scope and onboarding are invisible.
findings.fixSuggestion: Add a `README.md` to the repo root. At minimum: what the project does (one paragraph), how to run it, and a Features section listing key capabilities.

findings.title: Potential N+1 Query in while
findings.description:
`Ge.exec()` is invoked inside a `while` loop at aina-out/barnboard/app/static/js/htmx.min.js:1. Each iteration issues its own DB round-trip.
Line: var htmx=function(){"use strict";const Q={onLoad:null,process:null,on:null,off:null,trigger:null,ajax:null,find:null,findAll:null,closest:nu
findings.fixSuggestion: Batch the query: pre-build the id list, fire one query with `WHERE id IN (...)`, or use eager-loading (`.include()` / `.populate()` / `JOIN`). For parallelisation only, wrap in `Promise.all([...].map(...))` so the round-trips overlap.

agentic.resilienceLevel: Agent-Ready — Your API can handle 2000+ concurrent AI agents
failurePatterns: Cache-less architecture means 10 agents searching = 10x DB load for identical queries
Auth endpoint saturation: agents refreshing tokens every request = 2x load amplification
recommendations: Implement token bucket rate limiting (100 req/min per agent identity)
Add Redis caching with 30s TTL for all GET endpoints
Increase database connection pool to 50+ with PgBouncer
Add Retry-After headers and 429 status codes
Implement circuit breaker for external API calls
Paginate all list endpoints (max 50 items per page)
Rate limit auth endpoints separately (5/min)
Monitor for agentic traffic patterns (bursty, exploratory, retry-heavy)

findings.title: No Caching — Agents Will Repeat-Query Same Endpoints
findings.description: AI agents often re-query the same endpoints (list, search, detail). Without caching, every agent request hits the database — exponential load amplification.
findings.fixSuggestion: Add Redis caching with 30s TTL for list endpoints. Implement ETag/304 responses. Use CDN for static resources.

findings.title: Auth Endpoints Not Rate Limited
findings.description: AI agents frequently re-authenticate (token refresh, retry on 401). Without auth rate limiting, agents can brute-force or DoS your auth system.
findings.fixSuggestion: Rate limit auth endpoints separately: 5 attempts/min per IP. Add account locking after 10 failures. Monitor for unusual auth patterns.
